title: [AMD] Fix registered HiCache host pointer aliases (#35233)
body:
## Motivation

Registered HiCache host allocations can have different CPU and GPU virtual addresses. This is observable on MI355X, where `hipDeviceAttributeCanUseHostPointerForRegisteredMem` is false. Passing the CPU VA to a custom kernel causes a GPU memory fault even though runtime copy APIs can still accept that address.

The affected paths include AOT/JIT HiCache transfers, Mamba transfers, HiSparse copies, and host-pool pointer tables. CPU-side storage and disaggregation metadata must continue to expose the original CPU VA.

## Modifications

- Add a target-device-aware `get_device_accessible_ptr` AOT API using `cudaHostGetDevicePointer` / `hipHostGetDevicePointer`.
- Resolve direct registered-host tensor operands at AOT and JIT kernel launch boundaries while preserving the caller's current device.
- Build CUDA/ROCm host-pool kernel pointer tables from device-accessible aliases for MHA, MLA, K-only, DSV4 paged/state, and DSA pools.
- Keep raw CPU addresses for unregister, contiguous-buffer metadata, page metadata, and storage/disaggregation consumers.
- Preserve unpinned, NPU, and MUSA pointer behavior.
- Add registered-mmap regressions for pointer domains, AOT/JIT transfers, and CUDA graph capture/replay.

## Accuracy Tests

ROCm 7.2 / MI355X (`gfx950`), Docker image `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260813`:

- Fresh ROCm AOT build: passed.
- `test_hicache_page_first_write_back.py`: `15 passed`.
- `test_transfer_mamba.py`: `16 passed`.
- `test_hisparse.py`: `16 passed, 2 skipped`.
- `test_mem_pool_host.py`: `9 passed`.
- Registered-mmap post-rebase regressions: `3 passed`.
- Native HIP runtime comparison: alias matches `hipHostGetDevicePointer`; wrong-device input is rejected; current device is restored.
- Repository pre-commit hooks over the rebased PR diff: passed.

Not run. This is a correctness fix for registered-host pointer address domains; it does not change kernel bodies or transfer algorithms.

title: [Fix] Merge adjacent KV-row frees so a mid-page split under DCP cannot double-free (#38941)
body:
## Motivation

Radix-cache servers running hybrid Mamba + MLA models (Kimi-K3, Kimi-Linear) with `--dcp-size 8` crash under ordinary load:

```
mem_cache/allocator/base.py, free_segments
AssertionError: segment at 576 shares a page with the one ending at 576
```

Every scheduler dies at once. We hit it within a minute of an MMLU-style batch (many prefix-sharing logprob requests finishing together), and after a couple of hours of agentic traffic.

Here is what goes wrong. With decode context parallelism, the KV allocator's page is `page_size * dcp_size` (512 tokens at the defaults), and the radix tree correctly pages at that width. Cache-length caps, however, still land on the unwidened 64-token grid: the Mamba component caps a finished request's cacheable length at its last track boundary. When such a request finishes, `cache_finished_req` hands back its KV in two pieces, the page-unaligned tail and the deferred truncation tail, and the seam between them falls inside one 512-token page. `free_segments` has rejected segments that share a page since the shared-page assertion was added, so the scheduler asserts. Without the assertion it would be worse: the second piece would free a page the first piece already released.

## Modifications

The two pieces are contiguous, so they should be one free. `free_kv_row` now merges adjacent ranges before it builds segments (`coalesce_ranges` in `mem_cache/common.py`), and hands the allocator a single page-aligned range. Ranges with a gap between them that still share a page are left alone, so the allocator's assertion keeps protecting against real double frees.

The new unit test, `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_free_kv_row_coalesce.py`, drives `free_kv_row` on a paged allocator with the same shape scaled down (page 8, seam at 9). It fails with the assertion above on `main` and passes with this change. A second case checks that a genuinely shared page, with a gap between the ranges, is still rejected.

## Accuracy Tests

Kimi-K3 with `--attention-backend cutedsl_mla --dcp-size 8`, radix cache and hierarchical cache enabled, draft-model speculative decoding on. A benchmark run produced 210 prefill batches with radix hits and no assertions. Three servers on the same configuration without this change died within a minute of the same load.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: the change is one pass over a request's handful of free ranges at completion time.

body:
## Motivation

Fixes #38645 (related draft: #38790). On a PD decode node with `--dcp-size > 1`, `retract_decode` backs up the retracted request's KV through `MLATokenToKVPool.get_cpu_copy`, which indexes `kv_buffer` with the widened `req_to_token` ids. Ids past this rank's rows trip a CUDA device-side assert; in-range ones back up and restore the wrong token's row.

## Modifications

- `HostKVCache.maybe_dcp_kernel_indices` moves to `layers/dcp/layout.py` as a pure function `maybe_dcp_kernel_indices(indices, dcp_size, dcp_rank)` next to the other DCP index math; the HiCache MLA host pool and the PD retraction path both call it. Its whole-widened-page assert is dropped because a retracted prefix (`seqlen - 1` tokens) is ragged; the strided select only needs the run to start page-aligned. `test_ragged_run_is_rejected` goes with it.
- `MLATokenToKVPool.get_cpu_copy` / `load_cpu_copy` run their ids through it with `dcp_size = _write_loc_dcp_span`, so the unified pool's already-physical ids (`write_loc_is_dcp_resolved`) pass through untouched. Mamba/KDA state indices are not touched.
- Regression cases added to `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_decode_retraction_backup.py`: the DCP backup/restore round-trip fails on `main` with an out-of-range row index, and the resolved-pool case guards against double translation.

## Testing

- CPU unit tests: the new `TestDcpRetractionBackup` cases in `test_decode_retraction_backup.py` pass here and the round-trip case fails on `main`; `test_hicache_dcp_host_pool.py` index cases pass.
- 4xB200, Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B, PD TP2 prefill -> TP2/DCP2 decode (tokenspeed_mla, fp8 KV, page 64), forced retraction via `SGLANG_TEST_RETRACT=1 SGLANG_TEST_RETRACT_INTERVAL=6` on the decode node, 48 concurrent requests x 256 tokens, decode `--max-total-tokens 122880` so widened ids exceed the per-rank row count:
  - `main` (433c999d): CUDA `index out of bounds` device-side assert in `MLATokenToKVPool.load_cpu_copy` on the first round (~12 retractions in).
  - this branch: repeated 2-3 round runs, ~140-200 retractions each, no assert, all requests completed; per-token logprob delta vs a no-retraction reference within the batch-composition noise of a no-retraction rerun.
- Not addressed here: with forced retraction some resumed requests (~4/48 per round) degenerate into token repetition. This reproduces identically with `--dcp-size 1` on the same PD setup, so it is a separate retraction issue, not DCP.

title: dsv4.1: compression, KV I/O, and metadata kernels (#39652)
body:
## Summary
- Add `KVLayout` (`kernels/ops/attention/dsv4/kv_layout.py`, `include/sgl_kernel/deepseek_v4/kv_layout.cuh`): the paged FlashMLA main-KV formats as one enum with their per-token data / scale bytes, tile size and page alignment. `V4` is the existing 584-byte layout (448 fp8 nope + 64 bf16 rope + ue8m0 scales); `V41` (528 B, every dim fp8 with one ue8m0 scale per 32) and `V41_FP4` (288 B, e2m1 codes with one e4m3 scale per 16) are the DeepSeek-V4.1 formats. `PagedKV<layout, page_bits>::row` gives every writer the same address arithmetic, and `v41::store_row` is the single quantizer for the V4.1 rows.
- Thread `layout` through the existing cache writers and reader: `fused_store_cache` (with an optional in-kernel RoPE for the V4.1 layouts), `compress_norm_rope_store`, `fused_k_norm_rope_flashmla`, `dequantize_k_cache_paged`. The default stays `V4`, so current callers are unchanged.
- Add the ratio-1 / ratio-2 decode compressors (`csrc/deepseek_v4/c1.cuh`, `c2.cuh`, `ops/attention/dsv4/low_ratio_compress.py`): pair-pooling (ratio 2), RMSNorm, RoPE and the main-KV write in one launch, returning the pre-RoPE latent; `out_loc == 0` marks a padded graph row.
- Add the V4.1 dequantizers (`dequant_k_cache.py`), `fp4_utils.cuh` (e2m1 fake-quant helpers next to the existing `fp8_utils.cuh`), the pure-torch reference quantizer (`torch_quant.py`), and two small-batch metadata builders (`build_page_table_positions_small`, `build_low_ratio_metadata`).
- Model call sites (pool layout selection, the low-ratio compressor path) are in #38798.

## Changes to existing kernels
- `csrc/deepseek_v4/store.cuh`, `fused_norm_rope_v2.cuh`, `main_norm_rope.cuh`: the V4 path now addresses pages through `PagedKV`; same bytes as before. The kernel templates gain a `KVLayout` parameter.

- JIT builds of every layout variant of the touched kernels (c1, c2, store, compress norm-rope, main-K norm-rope) succeed.

title: [kv-shard 2/4] Sharded pools (#37615)
body:
## Motivation


This adds the KV pools that actually stripe.

Pool tensors keep their stock shape and size on every rank; only the written rows differ — each rank persists exactly the rows it owns under part 1's bijection. The consequence drives the whole design: during a sharded prefill, extend attention never reads the KV pool, because a rank's pool holds only its stripe of the prefix *and* of the current chunk. It reads a per-layer assembled scratch laid out `[prefix | chunk | trash]`, whose prefix region is NCCL-allgathered one layer ahead on a dedicated communicator and side stream. Part 1's rotated allocation makes a cached prefix's owners exactly cyclic, so that gather is a *regular* padded allgather with an owner-major output — no reorder pass.

Still unreachable at runtime: nothing constructs these pools, and the FA3 / trtllm_mla seams are `isinstance` no-ops on every existing configuration. Tests: 25 more CPU cases (plan capture, scratch translation vs a brute-force reference, write-path owner filter) plus a 2-GPU test that checks the assembled scratch is bit-exact on both the MLA and MHA axes.

## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4-Flash prefill on 4-way pipeline parallelism showed two avoidable sources of serialization on RTX 6000D (SM120): pipeline tensor communication ran through scheduler-stream synchronization, and the SM120 model path did extra work for attention output projection and SWA KV page repacking.

This PR overlaps PP tensor communication with compute and adds guarded SM120 fast paths for DeepSeek-V4. The new paths are disabled by default, or require an explicit SM120 opt-in, so unsupported configurations keep the existing behavior.

## Modifications

- Add a dedicated PP CUDA communication stream (`SGLANG_PP_COMM_OVERLAP`). Sends wait on the producer event on the communication stream instead of fencing the scheduler stream.
- Add vLLM-style lazy PP activation receive (`SGLANG_PP_VLLM_ASYNC_RECV`): metadata remains synchronous, tensor payloads use `irecv`, and `PPProxyTensors` waits only on first consumption. - Allow explicit FP8 `wo_a` on SM120 when the installed DeepGEMM exposes compatible `fp8_einsum` and UE8M0 scale-layout APIs.
- Add `SGLANG_OPT_SM120_DIRECT_SWA_KV`: retain 256-token logical allocator pages while storing SWA KV directly as 64-token physical pages consumed by the FlashInfer SM120 kernel, eliminating the per-layer 256-to-64 repack.

title: [kernel] Share the warp vectorized copy and enforce its alignment (#36176)
body:
> Generated by Claude.

## Motivation

Four JIT kernels hand-rolled the same thing: a warp cooperatively moving one contiguous row. `concat_mla`, `set_mla_kv_buffer`, `store_cache` and `set_mla_kv_concat_q` each had their own vector-width selection, their own tail handling, and their own idea of what alignment they required. `warp_inclusive_sum` existed in four separate copies.

That duplication was not just untidy — it hid a bug class. The vector width a copy picks is derived from the row **size** (a 1024 B row gets 16 B accesses), but the address it lands on is `base + index * stride`, and nothing constrains a stride to match the size. Two real faults came out of that gap during this work, both reproduced:

- a `kv_buffer` row stride of 1048 B (`ROPE_DIM=12`) took 16 B stores on odd `loc` → `CUDA error: misaligned address`
- `store_cache` with `num_threads=256` on a 100 B row silently dropped the last 4 B of **every** row, because `kKBytes / kNumSplit` truncated with no guard

## What changed

**One shared copy path.** `warp::load_bytes<kBytes, kPattern>` / `store_bytes` in `warp.cuh`, backed by `LoadStorePattern`. Handles arbitrary widths down to 1 byte, including odd ones, and the ragged tail. The four hand-rolled versions are gone.

**Alignment becomes a stated precondition, not an assumption.**
- `TensorMatcher::ensure_alignment(bytes)` validates the data pointer and every stride but the innermost (size-1 dims skipped, since their strides are arbitrary).
- `LoadStorePattern::get_vec_bytes` is now `SGL_DEVICE_HOST`, so the launcher and the kernel share **one** formula. Both previous faults traced to host and kernel each hand-rolling a different `gcd`.
- The `store_cache` split carries `static_assert(kKBytes % kNumSplit == 0)`, turning the silent truncation into a compile error.

**`warp::reduce` generalised.** `<kNumThreads, kInner>` → a symmetric `<kStart, kFinish>` bit range that expresses both old modes: `<N, 1>` is the old inner reduce, `<kFullWidth, N>` the old inter-group one. Verified against an independent reference on 9 configurations.

**New primitives.** `inclusive_reduce` / `inclusive_sum` / `_max` / `_min` (with `lane_id` defaulted so the segment-relative contract can't be got wrong), `broadcast`, `atomic::Event` (cross-CTA arrive/wait in one 32-bit word), and `bits.h`.

**`get_lane_id<N>()`, per platform.** Reads the lane register on CUDA — worth 8 instructions and 2 registers in a two-tile warp copy, because the modulo form makes the compiler re-derive the mask at every address scale. On HIP it masks `threadIdx.x`, since AMD has no la …[truncated]

title: [AMD] dsv4: pick kv_splits per index stream, not by occupancy alone (#39968)
body:
`_kv_splits_heuristic` splits only when the base grid underfills the device. That is the wrong question for the V4 sparse decode kernel. At bs=14 the grid nearly saturates (196 CTAs against a 384 target) so it picks splits=1, while the cost is set by ONE straggler CTA walking ~5,000 KV entries beside CTAs walking 200. Splitting breaks up that CTA; occupancy never sees it.

The discriminator is static and available at capture time: `compress_ratio`. CSA (ratio 4) is clamped to `index_topk`+128 = 1152 and is nearly uniform, so split-K loses on it (+5.1% at bs=14). HCA (ratio 128) is unclamped, kv_len is ~context/128 and reaches ~5,000, dispersion 0.70-0.78, and split-K wins at every kv_len the run traverses. Only HCA is overridden; SWA and CSA keep the existing heuristic.

`SGLANG_MLA_HCA_KV_SPLITS=0` restores the previous behaviour with no code change.

## Motivation

The MLA decode kernel sits at 1.2-3.1% of both the bandwidth and the flops roofline, so its cost is set by dispersion, not by the hardware: the batch's p50 token reads ~1,000 KV entries while its p99 reads ~3,100, and the kernel finishes when its slowest CTA does.

That dispersion lives in one of the three index streams. CSA (`compress_ratio` 4) is clamped to `index_topk`, so kv_len tops out at 1152 and the stream is nearly uniform. HCA (`compress_ratio` 128) has no such clamp — kv_len is ~context/128 and reaches ~5,000 at the ISL p99 of 634,941 — and `config.json` alternates the two per layer.

Split-K was previously set aside here because `_kv_splits_heuristic` reads only capture-time scalars and so cannot tell a ragged shape from a uniform one. That is true of the batch but not of the layer: `compress_ratio` is a static per-layer constant, so the discrimination is free.

The causal chain was tested under intervention before any of this was built, by clamping kv_len to 128 so the kernel does almost nothing: the step fell 17.07 ms at matched batch size against a pre-registered ~19.5. body:

## Motivation

GLM-5.2 could not run disaggregated PP prefill with MTP because:

1. PP + speculative decoding was rejected outside NPU even though the prefill path already forwards PP proxy tensors from stages that do not host the draft.
2. The NextN draft is hosted on the last PP stage and borrows the target embedding, but only the first PP stage materialized and loaded `embed_tokens`.
3. The PP ring dropped the draft model's DSA IndexShare seed (`dsa_topk_indices`), which could make decode ranks diverge between eager and CUDA-graph paths.

- Materialize and load `embed_tokens` on the last DeepSeek/GLM PP stage when speculative decoding is enabled.
- Preserve `dsa_topk_indices` through PP serialization and reconstruction.
- Map heterogeneous plain-MLA NIXL transfers through one destination-index dispatcher, while retaining layer-ID/positional pairing for other layouts.
- Add regression coverage for PP/MLA transfer mapping, PP/EAGLE validation, embedding ownership, and DSA seed round trips (including the `None` case).

title: [2/N] [Kernel] Fuse padding-preserving HiSparse slot translation (#39837)
body:
## PR stack

Merge in order:

1. [[1/N] [AMD] Fix HiSparse slot translation in the fused MLA KV writer](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38776)
2. [[2/N] [Kernel] Fuse padding-preserving HiSparse slot translation](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39837)

This PR builds on #38776. The first two commits carry that fix; review the final commit, which combines the kernel-fusion change and its CI registration, as this step of the stack.

## Summary

Keep the existing `translate_loc_to_hisparse_device()` API and use a single Triton kernel for one-dimensional CUDA and ROCm GPU slot lists. The kernel preserves padding, supports strided inputs, and produces a contiguous result for the AITER fused KV-cache writer.

## Why translation is needed

The model’s output locations identify tokens logically. HiSparse maps those locations to rows in its GPU cache, and the fused writer needs those physical row numbers.

Negative locations represent padding and must remain unchanged:

```text
Logical output locations:    [17, 18, -1]
                              |   |   |
HiSparse mapping:          17->3 18->5  padding
                              |   |   |
Physical write slots:        [ 3,  5, -1]
                              |   |   |
Fused KV writer:           row 3 row 5 skip
```

## Before

The fused writer calls the existing translation method, which directly indexes the mapping tensor:

```text
logical locations
       |
       v
mapping[locations]
       |
       v
make contiguous -> fused KV-cache write
```

This lookup also indexes the mapping for negative locations. For example, `-1` reads the mapping’s last entry, so preserving that padding marker depends on the sentinel stored there.

## After

Callers continue to use `kv_pool.translate_loc_to_hisparse_device(...)`. The pool selects the fused kernel internally for one-dimensional CUDA and ROCm GPU slot lists; scalar inputs, page tables, and CPU inputs retain the direct gather. The fused kernel handles valid locations and padding explicitly:

```text
For each logical location
           |
           +-> location >= 0: look up its physical slot
           |
           +-> location < 0:  keep the padding value unchanged
           |
           v
contiguous physical-slot tensor -> fused KV-cache write
```

The kernel reads the input using its actual stride and writes a contiguous output. It supports `int32` and `int64`, promoting the output type when the inputs differ, and leaves the original locations unchanged. Empty inputs return an empty output without launching the kernel.

title: [HiCache] TMA-staged host<->device KV transfer kernel (sm_90+) (#40278)
body:
**Before -> after** (HiCache host<->device KV transfer through the pool API, 8 layers x 32K tokens, GB300): H2D 97 -> 192 GB/s, D2H 93 -> 183 GB/s, about 2x, at the host link's copy-engine ceiling, using 4 of 152 SMs.

## Motivation

HiCache brings cached prefixes back from the pinned host pool into the device pool layer by layer, on a side stream, while the forward pass runs on the same GPU. Two properties of the transfer kernel therefore matter: how fast it moves a page, because the load gates the prefix hit, and how many SMs it takes from the forward pass to do so.

The register-staging JIT kernel in `hicache.cuh` is bounded by bytes in flight, not by the link. Each of its 1024 threads holds one 64 B slice of a row in registers between its load and its store, so a CTA has at most 64 KB outstanding at any time. With

```
bandwidth = bytes in flight / round trip
```

the measured ~48 GB/s per CTA on a GB300 (NVLink-C2C host link) corresponds to an effective host round trip of ~1.3 us. The copy-engine ceiling of the same link is ~210 GB/s H2D and ~192 GB/s D2H, so the default 2-block launch reaches ~90 GB/s, and saturating the link takes 6+ blocks of 1024 threads, every one of them issuing dependent loads for the whole transfer. Making the register pipeline deeper does not help: two rows in flight per thread measured 40 GB/s instead of 48, because at 1024 threads the extra registers cost more occupancy than the extra outstanding bytes buy.

TMA bulk copies remove that trade-off. One thread issues a 32 KB `cp.async.bulk` and the data lands in shared memory with no registers involved, so a single warp keeps a 192 KB ring in flight: three times the register kernel's outstanding bytes with nine warps per CTA instead of 32. Two hardware limits, measured with raw probe kernels on the same GPU, then set what any staged copy can reach:

| 1 SM probe | GB/s |
|---|---|
| stores to device memory (16 B vector stores or TMA bulk stores, 1 to 32 warps) | 66 |
| stores to pinned host memory | 53 |
| TMA bulk loads from host, 32 KB ops | 150-200 |
| TMA bulk loads, 512 B ops (one op per row) | 21 |

The SM write port (32 B/clk) caps one CTA around 66 GB/s in either design (Nsight Compute reports the L1-to-crossbar write peak as 4.86 KB/cycle for the whole GPU, i.e. 152 SMs x 32 B/clk, and a one-block store probe hits exactly that), and the TMA unit handles roughly one bulk op per ~50 cycles, which makes per-row bulk copies a trap. So no single-SM copy can reach the link. The design goal is therefore: run each CTA at its write port instead of at its load latency, and la …[truncated]

title: [Fix] Don't free the multi-CTAs KV counter the decode graphs captured (#39175)
body:
## Motivation

`DeepseekSparseAttnBackend._forward_trtllm` rebound the counter buffer:

```python
self._multi_ctas_kv_counter_buffer = grow_multi_ctas_kv_counter_buffer_if_needed(...)
```

`grow_..._if_needed` returns a **new** `torch.zeros` when it grows, so the assignment frees the buffer the decode CUDA graphs captured. Later replays write through a dangling pointer.

`batch_size` is `page_table_1.shape[0]` — **query rows, not requests** — so a *prefill* batch trips it, not decode. Reasoning in decode batch sizes (`max_running_requests x draft_tokens`) makes `TRTLLM_MLA_MAX_BATCH_SIZE=8192` look unreachable, which is why it hid.

Stock main, default flags, GLM-5.3-Flash tp4 / 4x GB300, 8192 in / 1024 out, temporary logging on all 4 ranks:

```
capture uses ptr=0xf0eb9d06dc00 bs=288      target-verify graph
capture uses ptr=0xf0e91ee00000 bs=48       draft-decode graph
grow fired: bs=16384 old_ptr=0xf0eb9d06dc00 new_ptr=0xf0e7c8e00000
            mode=EXTEND OLD_IS_THE_CAPTURED_ONE=True
```

Last capture ended 22 s before the first grow. Latent, not benign: a probe right after the grow did not land on the freed block, so today the stale writes hit memory nothing owns. Perturb the allocation pattern and it becomes a reproducible illegal access inside `fmhaSm100fKernel...DynamicTokenSparse`, the kernel that consumes the counter.

## Modifications

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `_multi_ctas_kv_counter_for` | oversized eager call takes a temporary; the captured allocation is never replaced |
| `_ensure_multi_ctas_kv_counter_capacity` | `init_cuda_graph_state` sizes for `max(max_bs, max_num_tokens)` before any capture; grow-only |
| class default `= None` | `init_cuda_graph_state` sizes it for every backend, but only the TRT-LLM branch allocates one |

Capture-time growth is then unreachable, and the assert guarding it is an invariant check rather than a live path.

Not applicable — buffer lifetime only, no numerics touched.

title: [kv-shard 3/4] Enable Control plane (#38468)
body:
## Motivation


This is the control plane: `--enable-kv-cache-sharding` plus the wiring that makes a prefill worker actually build the widened allocator and the striped pools and schedule against them.

The gate restricts the feature to PD prefill workers with fa3 (or trtllm_mla for plain-TP MLA), a real page size, and chunked prefill; picks the shard axis by topology (attention-CP under prefill CP, attention-TP for MLA without CP);
rounds `chunked_prefill_size` to the granule; and rejects each feature whose assumptions the striped pool breaks. On the scheduler side, capacity reporting and the `max_new_tokens` clamp widen by the shard size, and `PrefillAdder` charges one page per shard class and gates every admission on the assembly scratch, so a batch can never plan a gather larger than the scratch.

The flag is off by default and every seam branches on the resolved shard size, so a run without it takes byte-identical paths. **Note for the stack:** the P/D send filter lands in part 4, so the flag is not usable end to end until then.

### Admission uses the minimum owner capacity
The allocator exposes two different capacity numbers:

```text
available_size()      = N*p * min_r(F_r)   # conservative admission floor
aggregate_free_size() = p * sum_r(F_r)     # actual total free slots
```

The first represents capacity in complete owner cycles. The second is useful for accounting but cannot establish whether a particular cyclic extension fits.

For example, free-page counts `[0, 10, 10, 10]` contain 30 free pages in total, but cannot supply an extension that needs owner 0. The conservative floor is zero. It also rejects requests needing only the other owners, even though those requests could physically fit.

```text
W_i = N*p * ceil(K_i/N)
    = round_up(E_i, N*p)
```

```text
sum_i ceil(K_i/N) <= min_r(F_r)

equivalently:

sum_i W_i <= available_size()
```

```text

  + [W_i - round_up(E_i,p)]       # allowance for owner distribution

0 <= W_i - E_i < N*p
```

title: [3/N] elastic-ep: Recapture decode CUDA graphs after scale-up (#33723)
body:
## Summary

This PR follows [PR #30553](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30553)
and adds FULL decode CUDA graph recapture after runtime Elastic EP scale-up.
Primary and joiner ranks rebuild their graphs for the expanded topology before
the new EP size is committed.

The existing scale-up API and EPLB lifecycle are unchanged.

## Changes

- Defer initial decode graph capture on joining ranks until they enter the
  expanded world.
- Finish the current sampling step, release the old graph state, and rebuild
  decode graphs with the expanded Mooncake WORLD and NIXL rank mask.
- Require primary and joiner ranks to resolve the same graph mode and capture
  configuration before recapture.
- Reuse SGLang's existing FULL decode graph initializer and synchronize all
  ranks before committing the scale operation.
- Add graph-stable FA3 MLA metadata for the validated DeepSeek path.
- Reject execution modes that do not use the supported decode finalization
  path.

## Configuration

Launch primary and joiner groups with the same resolved graph settings:

```text
--cuda-graph-backend-decode full
--cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled
--cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 2 4 8 16
```

The scale request and status API are inherited from the base scale-up PR.

## Known Limitations

## Motivation

On gfx950, the absorbed q BMM and the fused RoPE + cat + KV write are two
separate launches -- `rocm_absorb_q_bmm` in prepare, `_fused_rope_cat_and_cache`
in core. At decode shapes neither fills half the CUs, so they run back to back
with most of the machine idle.

aiter ships `fused_fp8_bmm_rope_cat_and_cache_mla`, which does all three in one
grid. It is present at the pinned `AITER_COMMIT_DEFAULT` (`4ad9983`).

## What this does

`_can_fuse_bmm_rope_cat_and_cache` enumerates the conditions under which the
fused kernel is exactly equivalent to the two it replaces: gfx95 with AITER, an
fp8 absorbed weight, a rope to fuse, the skip-rope DSA path (`tilelang` or
`triton` backend), an absorb-capable attention backend, and no deep-gemm BMM,
experimental LoRA, or active `kv_b` LoRA. The caller adds `not q_replicate_active`
-- DCP all-gathers `q_nope_out` before core runs, and the fused path has none to
hand it. Anything else falls back to the two-launch path unchanged.

It also guards the new aiter import behind `is_gfx95_supported()`.
`rocm_linear_utils` is imported wherever AITER is on, gfx942 included, but the op

title: [Unified Cache] Dedup replicated MLA/DSA KV in the UMBP direct linker (#38778)
body:
## Motivation

The UMBP direct external linker suffixes every stored object key with `tp{rank}`:

```python
rank_suffix = f"tp{tp_rank}_cp{params.attn_cp_rank}_pp{params.pp_rank}"
self.storage.mla_suffix = rank_suffix
self.storage.mha_suffix = rank_suffix
```

For DeepSeek-V4 that stores `tp_size` byte-identical copies of every page. The DSv4/DSA device pools carry no `tp_size` term (`deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py` has no `tp_size`/`tp_rank` anywhere — per-token bytes are fixed, and MLA latent plus the DSA indexer are *replicated* across attention TP ranks rather than sharded), so all eight ranks in a TP8 run hold the same bytes and write them under eight different keys into one shared tier.

Nothing collapses them today:

- `offload()` -> `_run_offload()` calls `batch_put_ranges_from_ptr` with no pre-put existence check (`_page_exists` is wired only into the load path).
- `BackupKV` is dispatched from the replicated radix tree on every rank, so all ranks issue the write.
- The one dedup mechanism built for this case — the SharedSSDLeader/Follower scheme in `umbp_store.py`, gated on `is_mla_backend and tp_size > 1` — is deliberately disabled here via `per_rank_keyspace=True`, because a follower would look for keys the leader never wrote under the follower's own suffix.
- UMBP's own dedup is keyed on the key *string* (`RoutePutOutcome::kAlreadyExists`), so eight distinct keys never collide.

The per-rank suffix also makes the keyspace asymmetric against DP attention. `tp_cache_group` is the attention-TP group when DP attention is on (`kv_cache_builder.py`), which is size 1 for `tp8dp8`, so every DP rank already writes `tp0`. A DP-attention engine can therefore read what a plain-TP engine wrote, but not the reverse: ranks 1..7 look for `tp1..tp7`, which nobody wrote, and the MIN reduction in `UnifiedCacheLinkerWrapper._sync_restorable_prefix` (a 0/1 mask under MIN is an AND) then intersects the hit down to zero.

## Modifications

Add `_storage_suffix()`, mirroring the helper `MooncakeDirectLinker` already has: drop the `tp` term when `pool_group.rank_replicated`, so every rank names the same object. `cp` and `pp` always stay — CP shards the sequence and PP shards layers, so neither may be collapsed. The topology log line gains `rank_replicated` / `suffix`; its existing prefix is unchanged, since acceptance checks grep it.

**Only the key collapses — the write path is untouched, and every rank still writes.** `MooncakeDirectLinker` pairs its suffix helper with `offload_owner = not rank_replicated or tp_rank == 0`, which is safe there because MooncakeStore is  …[truncated]

title: [RL] Keep DSA cuda-graph state and the graph pool intact across TMS pause/resume (#40804)
body:
## Motivation

In RL colocation the engine releases the `GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_CUDA_GRAPH` torch-memory-saver region while the trainer runs and resumes it before the next rollout. Two things break on main:

1. The full-cuda-graph pool holds capture-time-initialized device state that replays read but never rewrite. Pausing discards it, so the first replay after resume reads garbage.
2. DSA's wide `page_table` (`max_num_tokens x max_ctx_len` int32) and the flashmla metadata stay resident during training even though they are rewritten in full before every replay.

## Modifications

- `FullCudaGraphBackend`: pass `enable_cpu_backup=True` to the memory-saver `cuda_graph` context so the pool is backed up on pause and restored on resume.
- `DeepseekSparseAttnBackend.init_cuda_graph_state`: allocate `page_table` and `flashmla_metadata` inside the pausable cuda-graph region (gated on `--enable-memory-saver` and `SGLANG_MEMORY_SAVER_CUDA_GRAPH`). The other decode metadata is written once at init and stays outside the region.

Squash of sglang-miles #32718, #33479 (authors credited as co-authors).

title: [HiCache] Add the page-unified KV load-back JIT kernel  (#39726)
body:
## Motivation
The load-back half of the page-unified HiCache layout, and the mirror of the staged write-back added in #39606. That PR writes a device pool out into host pages ordered

  MHA: (page, head_group, layer, 2, page_size, head_in_group, dim), K=0 V=1
  MLA: (page, layer, page_size, dim)

but stops at write-back; nothing could read those pages back. This kernel does, for one layer at a time.

Per-layer and unstaged, unlike its write-back mirror. The two directions are not symmetric in how the runtime drives them: write-back moves a whole page at once, so staging it on the device and handing the bulk copy to the copy engine costs nothing extra. Load-back is walked layer by layer by the L2 transfer engine, which unblocks the forward pass one layer at a time, so staging whole pages per layer would move num_layers times the bytes the layer actually needs. Instead the SMs read the pinned host mapping in place, the way every other layout's per-layer load already does.

Each thread moves 16 bytes; the linear index runs dim-fastest then item, so a warp's lanes read consecutive host bytes for the tokens of one (head group, layer, K/V) cell. The grid is capped by kBlockQuota as in HiCacheKernel: the load overlaps a forward pass, so extra blocks buy bandwidth by taking SMs from it.

Note that head_group == 1 is NOT page_first_direct's byte order -- the K/V axis sits inside the page block here, not outside the pool. The HG=1 cases in the test pin that.

Correctness: 123 cases pass on B200 -- 3 geometries x {uint8, fp16, bf16} x {int32, int64} indices x {0, 1, 8} tokens, for MHA and MLA, each sweeping every layer, compared for exact equality against a PyTorch-indexing reference including the rows that must keep their sentinel. Payload is seeded noise, not a counter: a counter is periodic in the layer stride, so a layer mix-up would compare equal.

Round-trip against #39606: running that PR's write-back and then this kernel over 9 configurations (including the head-cut cases) returns the device pool bit-identical, which is the actual contract between the pair.
